doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Taking on advanced students; growth of the New School program
summary: He takes only good players, not beginners; enrollment has grown from under 50 to over 200.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: classes. And I’m still doing private teaching. And that I like. You know I never thought I would like it so much. A couple of my colleagues asked me to try it, and I’ve been at it ten years now, as an adjunct.
Do you take on students who already play piano?

I do. I don’t take on beginners, no. Because that I’m not very experienced, in teaching anybody in the very beginning. When I try to think about myself I think, I was unusual. I don’t want to teach anyone like me. But no, most of the students that I get are really good players. I’m able to select them. And the blues classes are great too. We still get people from everywhere, I mean all over the world. I think, when I started, last time I talked to you I think our enrollment was, oh under 50 people. Now it’s over 200.
